reader.requirement: At COBOL-85, a NUMVAL-C reference without argument-2 must take cs to be the program's currency symbol: the single character of the CURRENCY SIGN clause when present (§1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11), else the currency sign $ (§1985:III.2), and an explicit argument-2 replaces it.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry NumvalCLocalePhrase2002 / NumvalCAnycaseKeyword2002 (refused at 85; a data item named LOCALE is an operand) and DialectBehavior.NumvalCCurrencyContentRules (off at 85)
CurrencySymbolExclusion.For(DialectLevel) and CurrencySymbolEquivalence.Fold(DialectLevel): the 1985 GR11 exclusion list; the PICTURE SYMBOL phrase is a 2002 construct

reader.edition-search: SoleCurrencyString itself is edition-blind (0 explicit strings gives $, 1 gives that string); the edition shapes which CURRENCY clauses can exist at 85, and BindNumvalCFamily injects the sole string as argument-2
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the currency string is one character (GR11) and argument-2 content is unscreened; the injection of the program's currency symbol as cs is the same code
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf41_05 (CURRENCY SIGN '#') and g85_bf41_06 (default $) cover the leading-cs forms; not a letter currency symbol, an explicit argument-2 that overrides the program symbol, a value with no cs, the cs/DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA combination, or the 2002 multi-character and PICTURE SYMBOL forms 85 must refuse

probes.expected: '#' as cs under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA

probes.printed: COBOL0890 CURRENCY SIGN "EUR": without PICTURE SYMBOL the literal shall consist of a single character
probes.expected: refused: 'limited to a single character' (§1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11)

probes.printed: COBOL0893 CURRENCY SIGN WITH PICTURE SYMBOL requires COBOL-2002
COBOL2423 clause written 2 times (format admits it once) and COBOL1644 2 distinct currency strings
probes.expected: refused: the 1985 SPECIAL-NAMES format admits one CURRENCY SIGN clause

probes.printed: COBOL0891 CURRENCY SIGN literal 'R': not a valid currency symbol (ISO §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11)

probes.expected: at 85 LOCALE is a user word: a data item LOCALE VALUE '#' is argument-2, so '#5' = 5

reader.notes: The binder injects the unit's sole currency string ($ by default, else the CURRENCY SIGN character) as argument-2 when none is written, and every probed form returns the represented value. Lead outside this slice (1989-AR-A.2.30.3-1 / AR4): lead_nc_class.cob in the scratch directory shows a PIC A argument-2 and a numeric-edited argument-1 refused with COBOL1627 at 85, while §1989:A.2.2 type 3 admits 'A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric'; site IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Admissible ('a' kind) and #PredicateViolation (CharacterCategory).

refuter.evidence: Attacked the program-currency injection (SoleCurrencyString) for an inherited symbol and for a 1985-only symbol. nest_nc.cob: the contained program inherits CURRENCY SIGN '#' and NUMVAL-C('#1.234,5') with no argument-2 gives 1234.50 (MATCH); sep_nc.cob: separately compiled SEPB without the clause takes '$' ('$1,234.5'=1234.50, MATCH). cur_n.cob: CURRENCY SIGN IS 'N' (not excluded by §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11 list b) is accepted at 85 and NUMVAL-C('N12.50CR')=-12.50, NUMVAL-C(' - N 1,003')=-1003.00 (MATCH). Incidental, outside this rule: NUMVAL-C of a numeric-edited item is refused with COBOL1627 citing the 2023 CATEGORY wording, the reader's AR1/AR4 lead. cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.30.3 AR5  (2.30.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR5'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR11  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR11'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.2  (4.2 CONFIGURATION SECTION)  the text is in the clause'.
